cohort: The study included women aged 18-40 years with high-risk pregnancies and a gestational age of more than 28 weeks, who received emergency obstetric care.
finding: The provision of early triage and emergency obstetric care for high-risk pregnancies was associated with no observed maternal mortality and morbidity, a 99.9% live birth rate, 0.7% early neonatal deaths, and one intra-uterine death.
mod_finding: The majority of participants (94.3%) were delivered by cesarean section due to obstetric reasons.
followup_time: Up to the early neonatal period (typically 7 days postpartum) for fetal outcomes.
